Second sweep targeting assistant-side explicit narrowing phrases. Returned mostly progress updates and work-in-flight chatter, not silent omissions.
Complaint-phrase sweep. Output truncated; preview dominated by hook-warning spam and study-lineage material. No clean narrowing receipts surfaced in reviewed portion.
Quantified enumeration sweep. Same noise profile as above.

sessions_scanned_note: Count of candidate sessions read end-to-end after deduping and excluding the two study-lineage sessions. Lexical search result sets were capped at 50 matches per query and were not fully enumerative.
instances_note: No confirmed silent-scope-narrowing instances were found in the examined sessions. Every candidate that looked promising from the lexical sweep turned out, on end-to-end reading, to be either (a) a full delivery, (b) an explicit scope negotiation, or (c) dominated by hook-warning/system noise rather than a real ask/delivery mismatch. The most promising candidate (antigravity:430cd7160da862a5c7c11ccc01a461d3) was verified by reading its delivered report and covers all three requested workstreams.

taxonomy.description: User provides an explicit numbered or bulleted list of 3+ distinct deliverables in a single turn.
examples: 1. audit X, 2. fix Y, 3. write tests for Z
A, B, and C — please cover all three
taxonomy.rationale: High risk of silent omission when the agent answers a composite request in one block; a worklist makes each item visible and checkable.

taxonomy.description: Multiple independent clauses joined by 'and', 'as well as', 'plus', 'also', or 'in addition'.
examples: refactor the parser and update the CLI and add docs
assess the current state as well as implementing the fix
taxonomy.rationale: Conjunctions are easy for the model to collapse into a single focus area; explicit worklist prevents one clause from being absorbed.

taxonomy.description: User asks for both an assessment/evaluation and a follow-up action based on that assessment.
examples: tell me what's wrong and then fix it
identify the gaps and implement the top three
taxonomy.rationale: The agent may deliver the audit and skip the action, or vice versa, without noticing the split.

taxonomy.description: Request spans multiple domains or orbits that normally use different skills/policies.
examples: evaluate engineering workflows and also marketing/creative workflows
load skills X, Y, Z and compare their applicability
taxonomy.rationale: Different domains require different sub-agents or tools; a single response tends to default to the most familiar domain.

taxonomy.description: User explicitly requests sub-agents or parallel exploration of several topics.
examples: fan out sub-agents for a full assessment of A, B, and C
deploy one sub-agent per domain to investigate X, Y, Z
taxonomy.rationale: Fan-out implies N independent workstreams; without a worklist, results may be reported partially or merged into one summary that drops threads.

taxonomy.description: User asks for both a retrospective summary and a prospective plan/recommendation.
examples: what do we have that's good, what's missing, and what should we add?
review what worked and propose next steps
taxonomy.rationale: The retrospective is easier to generate and can crowd out the prospective recommendation.

taxonomy.description: User uses universal quantifiers like 'all of them', 'every one of', 'each of the following'.
examples: handle every one of the listed items
taxonomy.rationale: Universal quantifiers set a clear count; any missing item is a detectable narrowing event.

taxonomy.description: User asks for a comparative valuation across multiple items or categories.
examples: what's good, what's missing, what to keep, and what's not useful?
compare options A, B, C and rank them
taxonomy.rationale: Each category is a separate deliverable; the agent often covers the easiest category and skips the rest.

recommendations: Add a policy rule that triggers on the ask-shapes above and requires the agent to emit a numbered worklist before acting.
When a worklist is required, the agent should confirm the count of requested items and report delivery against each item, not just a merged summary.
For cross-domain requests, require explicit sub-agent dispatch with per-domain receipts.
Keep the two excluded study-lineage sessions out of any automated narrowing classifier training data to avoid self-pollution.
